en: It's the latest version of Inner Fighter! I call it Inner Fighter 8: Road Battle, or IF8 for short!
Indeed! It's my brand new game machine that uses special electromagnetic waves to let you experience realistic fights within your very mind.
Sounds like a recipe for brain cancer.
No no, there's nothing dangerous about it. In fact, playing it can actually help you.
Says the mad scientist...
If you don't believe me, try it for yourself. Then you'll truly see the wonder that is IF8!
You could play right now if you'd like, of course.
Don't be so quick to judge. I've been working on this arcade machine for many years.
Oh, you must be Minamida. Your assistant in Kineicho was pestering me about playing this thing.
So you've met my assistant? I take it you're up to speed, then?
(This old guy's got shady written all over him.)
One more thing. IF8 is not finished yet. We'll need to sink a lot more money into it before it'll be done.
That's where you come in! We're hoping you'll help us with the necessary funds. You see, I may not look it, but I'm flat out broke.
You'll benefit as well, because once it's complete, it will feed back a variety of data to you whenever you play.
So please consider making an investment. It'll be well worth your while!
All we need is a little more data, and you'll be able to play in other towns. You'll have to be patient until then.
One more thing... As I mentioned before, IF8 is not finished yet. We'll need to sink a lot more money into it before it'll be done.
Tsukimino? All right, that will be 10,000 yen.
Sotenbori? All right, that will be 10,000 yen.
Kineicho? All right, that will be 10,000 yen.
All right, let me explain flashback battles to you.
In flashback battles, you fight powerful enemies from your past.
IF8 faithfully recreates the battle based on your memories.
Only some enemies are available, though. And you won't gain weapon proficiency or experience, so remember that!
But if you win, there will be a nice little surprise for you, just as with the road battles.
The cost to play is the same, too. 10,000 yen.
Would you care to play?
Flashback Battles cost 10,000 yen to play. Care to play?
All right, that will be 10,000 yen.
Let the Flashback Battle commence!
Oh, all right then. I'll be here in case you feel like playing later.
You got a <Color:8>Mystery Liquid<Color:Default>.
You got a <Color:8>Small Motor<Color:Default>.
You got a <Color:8>Snowman Hammer<Color:Default>.
You got a <Color:8>Gravity Converter<Color:Default>.
There's a weird old man in a white coat at the bottom of the escalator down there.
I'd stay away from him if I were you. He keeps talking about this thing called inner something-or-other. Talk about expensive!
You better pay up quick!
(What's going on here?)
Please! Just a little bit longer!
The money's due now. Stiff us again, and we'll be taking this place off your hands as payment!
No, not that...! I promise I'll pay all the money I owe soon!
Bah... Let's bounce.
Okay, boss!
Man... What now? There's no way I can put together that much money.
Everything okay? I noticed you had some trouble earlier.
I'll be fine... Oh, who am I kidding? There's no way I'm getting out of this mess.
Has business been bad or something?
Mm, you could say that. We've been running this café in Kamurocho for years now, and one way or another, we've made ends meet. But then I went and got greedy.
I decided to open up branches in Sapporo and Nagoya, and they haven't been doing well.
Even though business did start picking up there after what seemed like forever, I'm still up to my eyeballs in debt from the opening costs.
The branch here in Kamurocho does turn a little profit, but not enough to pay the interest.
So that's how it is...
At this rate, it won't be long before those moneylenders take my café away. They'd have every right to do it, too.
If only I could come up with a really special dish that brought in droves of customers... That's about all that could save me now.
But life isn't that simple, is it? *sigh*
(So he needs a miracle on his menu. Hmm...)
Oh, hello? It's me, Tatsuya.
Is that you, Suzuki-san?
Uh, yes. What's going on? Something I can help you with?
No, it's just that I'm in Kamurocho right now, and I wanted to get you a gift for helping me back in Fukuoka.
Any Tokyo specialties you like in particular?
Actually, I'm in Kamurocho now myself.
What, you are!? What a coincidence! I guess it was meant to be, then!
We should definitely meet up while we're both in the area!
I'll be at Theater Square. Come and see me when you can! Bye!
(Maybe Tatsuya can think of a dish that would save this place.)
(He said he was at Theater Square. I'll go meet him and see what he thinks.)
Hey! It's been a while, huh? How have you been doing?
(Maybe Tatsuya can think of a dish that would save Café Alps.)
Oh, there was something I wanted to ask you.
...I think I get the picture. He needs something tasty enough to get his business booming before time runs out.
I know you're busy, but do you think you can come up with anything?
Hmm, that's going to be tricky. I really wish I could help out.
<Color:40>But I'm still doing that project where I visit regional restaurants around the country.
<Color:40>Until I finish that, I won't be able to tackle anything new, I'm afraid.
<Color:1>I see. Sorry to ask such a big favor.
<Color:40>No worries. Once I'm done with my stuff, that café is the first place I'll head to!
<Color:1>Great. That'd be appreciated. I'll see you around then.
<Color:40>(Tatsuya is traveling the country developing new dishes for restaurants. He won't be able to help until that's finished.)
Welcome to...  Whoa! No way!
It's Tatsuya-san! The culinary crusader of Japan is here to visit <Italic>me</Italic>!?
Wait, you know him?
Of course I do! Practically everyone in the restaurant trade does! He's famous nationwide!
Oh, you flatter me. Hahaha.
But what are you doing in a dingy old café like this, Tatsuya-san?
Actually, I asked him to help you out. I didn't want to see the place go under.
You did? Really!? Thank you! And, Tatsuya-san, you're willing to help me turn this place around?
Let's just say I owe a favor to Suzuki-san. Now then. Allow me to work my magic and whip up the ultimate comfort food! This place will never be the same again!
I can't believe this is happening! Thank you!
Okay, then let's get started. You don't mind if I borrow your kitchen, do you?
Go right ahead!
Ah, Suzuki-san! Good to see you! How are things?
Fair. How about you?
Oh yes. After meeting you in Nagasu, I traveled to Tsukimino, Sotenbori, and Kineicho looking for tasty local delicacies.
Now I have a ton of amazing recipe ideas swimming through my mind's eye. I'm getting the urge to create something new and exciting!
That's good... Listen, about that, I actually had a favor to ask you.
A favor? Such as?
I see... He needs something tasty enough to get his business booming before time runs out.
I know you're busy, but do you think you'd be able to come up with something?
Sure, I'd be glad to help! You just leave it to me.
Okay, no time to waste! Let's head to this café!
You've been a big help, Tatsuya. This is all thanks to your recipe.
Yes, with the way things are looking, I think we have a fighting chance! I really can't thank you enough!
No thanks required. This was a good chance to get a few of the ideas I had out of my head. And you know what? I think it turned out great.
Oh, why don't you try it while you're here, Suzuki-san?
You don't mind?
Of course not! Go on, have a seat!
This is the culmination of everything I learned from the people and the food of Nagasu, Tsukimino, Sotenbori, Kineicho, and Kamurocho.
I call it... the Ultimate Napolitan!
The Ultimate Napolitan, huh? That's quite a name to live up to.
Yes indeed. You know as well as I do, Napolitan spaghetti is a fixture at many Japanese cafés. This is my take on that old classic.
Instead of regular sausage, I use the salsiccia you often find in Italian dishes, and instead of plain old mushrooms I went with porcini.
That lends the dish the same rich aroma that you'd experience in a high-class Italian restaurant.
I also use Parmesan cheese and honey as accents, and these bring out even more of that sweet, gooey flavor.
That sounds amazing. Can I try it?
Of course! I want you to taste the medley of flavors that my culinary pilgrimage inspired.
Wow... All we did was spread a few flyers about Tatsuya-san crafting our new dish, and look at the turnout! I can hardly believe my eyes!
Incredible, isn't it?
Yeah! Let's go check it out inside!
Oh, sure.
I can't even begin to thank you, Tatsuya-san.
Like I said, no thanks necessary. If you want to thank someone, thank Suzuki-san here.
Right. If I hadn't met you, I would never have come up with such a unique creation.
You were kind enough to show me around Nagasu when I was in a fix. Even though you were busy, you took me all over town.
And it's not just you. In every town I visited, there were people willing to help me out of the kindness of their hearts. It was truly touching.
So now I want to pay some of that kindness forward.
Tatsuya...
This recipe was based on the warmth and goodwill I felt from those who supported me.
That's what makes it the ultimate dish. The experiences I've had taught me that.
After all, what better way to season a dish than with a little love and gratitude?
So being thankful is the ultimate seasoning... Heh, I guess I could see that being the case.
I get the feeling this has really helped me grow as a chef. I won't run out of recipe ideas anytime soon, that's for sure.
In fact... I can feel another dish calling to me, just waiting to be created! Time is precious, so I'd best be on my way!
After all, I want to show my gratitude to as many people possible!
That's a great attitude to have. I'm sure everyone's looking forward to what you'll come up with next.
I hope so! Well, I've got to get going. Until we meet again!
(I bet he has plenty more delicious dishes left in that creative mind of his. Good luck, Tatsuya.)

Tatsuya's Ultimate Napolitan was added to the Café Alps menu
at the Kamurocho branch.
You got 3,000 experience points.
Come on, Santa! We want presents!
*pant* Geez, I'm spent. That's enough Santa for me!
Hey, you all right?
Urgh... I got beat up by a gang of Santa hunters.
Santa hunters? Look, can you just tell me if you're all right?
Yeah, I think so.
Well, you can stand, at least. That's a good sign.
Yes, sorry to have troubled you.
No worries. But what was that ya said earlier? Somethin' about Santa hunters?
They're a gang of delinquents. They make a game of beating up retail workers wearing Santa costumes.
Wow. Buncha punks...
Because of them, people don't consider the shopping district a safe place anymore. It ruins the festive mood entirely.
I'll give those kids a talkin' to.
Pardon? You're going to, what, lecture them? How?
They go after Santas, right? Lend me your outfit.
You're going to use yourself as bait? That's nuts. They've got close to ten kids. By yourself, you couldn't possibly...
Wasn't plannin' on fightin' them. They might just listen to reason.
I doubt that...
Don't worry. If things get ugly, I'll cut and run. I won't push it.
That's rough. Just gotta hope they'll regret it when they're older, right? But I gotta go now.
Oh. Okay, then.
Urff... Those punks...
Santa hunters, eh? Dumb kids.
All right. This should make the Santa hunters come lookin' for me.
Please be careful. They carry weapons, and they're not shy about using them.
I'll be fine.
(All right, let's find these so-called Santa hunters.)
Look, it's Santa again! Do you have my present now?
Oh, oh! What about me?
Santa! I want my present!
You all are just begging to end up on Santa's naughty list!
Hey, it's Santa!
Yaaay!
(Hehe, cute kids. Wearin' this getup around town ain't so bad!)
Santa, can I have my present now?
Sorry, tykes, ain't got nothin' on me. At least not stuff that would make good gifts for ya.
Huh? No fair! I want my present!
Pweeease, Santa!
No presents. I don't got my... uh, sleigh with me.
Why didn't you bring it!?
Look, it's Santa! I want a present!
What? Santa? *gasp* He's here!
Santa, can I sit on your lap?
Do you have a present for <Italic>me</Italic>?
